diagnosed_skill_and_repair.overall_diagnosis: Verifier failures stem from gaps in the lab-unit-harmonization skill’s analyte-specific unit inference and conversion guidance for mixed SI/conventional datasets. The skill appears to cover general harmonization and some common CKD labs, but lacks a comprehensive conversion catalog, clear physiologic-range/threshold heuristics per analyte, and iterative post-conversion validation—leading to missed or incorrect conversions for bilirubin fractions, thyroid hormones, lipids (including subfractions), iron studies, and other edge-case assays such as troponins and blood gases.

skills.name: lab-unit-harmonization
skills.heading: Lab Unit Harmonization
skills.diagnosis: The skill is too generic for row-level unit inference in real-world mixed-unit lab columns and is missing/underspecified conversion factors and heuristics for several analytes repeatedly failing verification (bilirubin total/direct, Free T4/Free T3, cholesterol fractions and other lipids, iron studies, plus common edge cases like blood gases and troponins). As a result, range-triggered logic either fails to trigger (overlapping plausible ranges) or applies incorrect factors, leaving values outside expected physiologic ranges.
skills.repair_instruction: Add a task-oriented ‘analyte conversion playbook’ that includes, for each benchmark-relevant analyte: (1) canonical target unit (US conventional vs SI) and expected physiologic range(s) used for plausibility checks; (2) bidirectional conversion factors and common source units; (3) explicit unit-inference thresholds/heuristics for mixed-unit columns (row-level conversion) including overlapping-range cases. At minimum cover: Total/Direct Bilirubin (µmol/L↔mg/dL; factor 17.1), Free T4 (pmol/L↔ng/dL; factor 0.0777), Free T3 (pmol/L↔pg/mL; factor 0.651), lipid panel and subfractions LDL/HDL/Non-HDL/Triglycerides (mmol/L↔mg/dL; cholesterol factor 38.67; triglycerides factor 88.57), serum iron (µmol/L↔µg/dL; factor 5.585). Extend with edge-case sections for blood gases (kPa↔mmHg; factor 7.5006), troponins (ng/L↔ng/mL and related reporting conventions), lactate, urine chemistries, and protein markers. Finally, specify an iterative workflow: infer units → convert selectively → validate against ranges → if still implausible, reclassify/try alternate unit mapping → flag for manual review. Include examples of mixed-unit datasets and cautions against blanket conversions (especially lipids) without analyte-specific thresholds.
